title: Counterfactual Istidlal — the Introduction
description: A small, carefully curated set of counterfactuals. Answers link directly to the Qur'anic, hadith, and book references used in the reasoning. The hypothetical conclusion is an inference, not a claim that the source explicitly answered this exact question.

coverage.selection_policy: Curated for distinct learning value; no quota per concept.

book-u01.work: A Survey into the Lives of the Infallible Imams
book-u01.author: Murtadha Mutahhari
book-u01.locator: Introduction: A Comparison between Imam al-Husayn's Path and That of Other Imams

counterfactuals.prompt: If every Imam had followed the same visible political strategy in every era, would that necessarily have produced greater fidelity to Islam?
counterfactuals.answer: Not necessarily. The introduction's argument is that the Imams faced different threats and opportunities while preserving the same core commitments. [Qur'an 22:39](https://quran.com/22/39) connects permission to fight with being wronged; it does not prescribe identical action in every circumstance. The chapter's account of al-Husayn's revolt and other Imams' restraint therefore asks us to judge a strategy against its conditions and purpose, not to turn one historical response into a universal script. The inference is about contextual judgment; it does not mean convenience can override principle.
counterfactuals.istidlal_takeaway: A stable moral purpose can require different outward strategies when circumstances and duties differ.

counterfactuals.prompt: If an Imam narrated a Prophetic practice but did not personally follow it in a later era, should we assume he contradicted the Prophet?
counterfactuals.answer: Not before asking whether the practice was a permanent command or a response to a particular circumstance. Mutahhari uses the beard-dyeing example to distinguish outward form from underlying purpose. [Qur'an 16:90](https://quran.com/16/90) gives enduring moral principles—justice and good conduct—while a specific historical tactic may have a narrower purpose. The passage supports careful interpretation, not a license to dismiss any inconvenient report: the context and evidence must establish whether a ruling is general or situational.
counterfactuals.istidlal_takeaway: Before calling a contradiction, distinguish the lasting principle from a context-specific application.
